S01.headline: High blood pressure doesn't feel like anything.
S01.sub: That's the whole problem with it. SteadyBeat helps you see your own numbers and your own habits, and hand them to someone who can actually read them.

blocks.title: Your readings stay yours
blocks.body: Nothing goes to your practice unless you send it, and you see the exact file before it leaves.

blocks.title: A number can mean call someone
blocks.body: Some readings, and some feelings, are a phone call rather than a log entry. We say which, and we say it before you tap save.

blocks.title: You will never get a score out of this
blocks.body: No ten-year figure, no letter, no green tick or red light on your reading. Working out what your numbers mean together is a consultation, and we are not one.

S01.footer: Education and self-management support. Not a diagnosis or treatment.

S02.title: What it does
S02.headline: Four moments this is built for.
S02.sub: Not four features. Four points where a heart condition you can't feel becomes something you have to act on.

blocks.title: When the cuff has been in the drawer since March
blocks.body: A week of just taking readings, nothing asked of you. Seven mornings is a picture. One morning is a mood.

blocks.title: When the habit is the hard part, not the knowledge
blocks.body: You already know about walking and salt. One aim, set by you, small enough to survive a bad week.

blocks.title: When a reading comes back higher than usual
blocks.body: The screen tells you what would make it urgent and who to ring. It does not tell you what the number means.

blocks.title: When you're sitting in the waiting room with nothing to show
blocks.body: A month of readings, in one file, that you choose to send. Your practice sees what you sent and nothing else.

blocks.title: What it isn't
blocks.body: It doesn't read your cuff, name a medicine, change one, calculate an assessment of you, or grade a reading. If a screen ever looks like it's doing one of those, it's a bug worth reporting.

S02.footer: Education and self-management support. Not a diagnosis or treatment.

S03.title: Consent & privacy
S03.headline: What we hold, and what we don't.

blocks.title: Held on your phone
blocks.body: Your readings, the home number you typed in, your check-ins, your notes, your walking aim. These stay local.

blocks.title: Shared with your practice
blocks.body: Nothing, until you choose. When you do, you read the whole file first — and the file has no mood ratings and no notes in it.

blocks.title: You can leave
blocks.body: Export or delete everything at any point. Deletion is completed, not hidden — your phone, our servers, and anything waiting to sync.

items.title: Let June see that I'm using this
items.body: Off by default. She'd see that you're here, and nothing you logged.

blocks.title: One thing you are not consenting to
blocks.body: This is not monitoring. Nobody is watching your readings, including us, and nothing here can call an ambulance for you. If something is wrong now, use the phone.

S03.footer: You can change either choice later in Settings.

S04.title: Baseline week
S04.headline: Just take the readings.
S04.sub: Nothing changes this week. No aim, no nudge. One reading each morning, the same way each time, so the week means something.

blocks.title: Same chair, same arm, before coffee
blocks.body: Sitting, feet on the floor, arm resting at about the height of your heart, five quiet minutes first. This isn't fussiness — it's the difference between a week you can compare and a week you can't.

blocks.title: These are numbers you typed in
blocks.body: SteadyBeat doesn't read your cuff and doesn't check what you enter. Home readings also aren't clinic readings, and we never mix the two into one line.

blocks.title: You don't have to wait out the week
blocks.body: Set your aim now if you'd rather. We'll mark the baseline as partial and say so on every chart that uses it.

blocks.title: If a reading worries you this week
blocks.body: Don't wait for the baseline to finish. There's a list of what makes a reading urgent, and a number to ring.

S05.title: Your weekly aim
S05.headline: What could you actually do next week?
S05.sub: Pick something that survives a bad Tuesday. You can move it later, in either direction, with no penalty.

blocks.title: Minutes of walking, on the mornings you walk
blocks.foot: Short and repeatable beats long and occasional, for most people, most of the time.

blocks.title: Mornings a week
blocks.foot: Four leaves you three days of slack before the week is spoiled.

blocks.title: One change to the evenings
blocks.body: Optional, and one is plenty. Most of the salt in a week arrives in food somebody else cooked.
chips: Takeaway once instead of three times

blocks.title: We are not setting a blood pressure target
blocks.body: There's no slider here for your numbers, and there never will be. The home number on your reading screen is the one your clinician gave you and you typed in. Only you can change it, and changing it here changes nothing about your care.

S05.footer: Loosening an aim takes effect straight away. Nothing here waits or argues with you.

S06.headline: Your plan is ready.
S06.sub: Have a last look. Any line here can be edited now or later.

blocks.title: Light — one reading, four walks
blocks.body: We'll suggest more only if your own numbers say it would help, and you can say no.

S08.title: Daily check-in
S08.headline: How did today go?
S08.sub: No right answers, and nothing here is a test. It only shapes what we offer you next.

blocks.title: How did the habits go?
blocks.body: A week where you manage some of it is a normal week, not a bad one.

blocks.title: Medicines as usual today?
blocks.body: Yes or no is all we record. We never ask which ones or how much, and we never tell you what to take or when to change anything.

blocks.title: How heavy did today feel?
blocks.foot: This is how the day felt to you. It is not a measurement of anything.

blocks.title: Anything going on today?
chips: Out of breath on the stairs

blocks.title: Some things don't belong in a check-in
blocks.body: Chest pain or pressure. Trouble speaking or understanding. Weakness or numbness down one side. A drooping face. Sudden trouble seeing, or a sudden severe headache unlike your usual. Breathlessness at rest. Any of those, right now, is 911 — not a chip, and not something to finish this screen first.
Everything on this screen is you describing your own day. SteadyBeat records it as a self-report, never as a clinical finding, and never adds it up into an assessment of you.

S08.footer: Private · Works offline · You can edit today's answers later

S09.title: Readings
S09.headline: What did the cuff say?
S09.sub: One reading, both numbers, and the time. That's all that goes in.

blocks.eyebrow: The number is yours, not ours
blocks.title: Under 135 over 85, at home
blocks.body: You typed this in on 12 February from your appointment. SteadyBeat didn't choose it, can't change it, and has no view about whether it's right for you. Home numbers usually sit lower than clinic ones, which is why this is a separate line from anything measured at the practice.

blocks.title: When a reading is a phone call
blocks.body: If a reading is well above what you normally get, sit quietly for five minutes and take it again — a single high number is often a single high number. If the second one is still well above your usual, ring the practice today and read them both out. We will not tell you what either one means.

blocks.title: Don't wait, and don't take it again
blocks.body: Chest pain or pressure. Trouble speaking. Weakness or numbness down one side, or a drooping face. Sudden trouble seeing, or a sudden severe headache unlike your usual. Breathlessness at rest. With any of those, the reading stops mattering — call 911.
This screen shows your reading and how it's been moving. It does not grade it, colour it, or work out what it means. Typed in by you, unchecked by us.

S09.footer: Saves offline · You can edit or delete any reading here

S10.headline: Short, plain, and dated.
S10.sub: Seven pieces, none longer than a bus ride. Each one shows when it was last checked.

GETTING A USABLE READING AT HOME

THE SIGNS THAT MEAN 911, LEARNED BEFORE YOU NEED THEM

blocks.title: Named, not added up.
blocks.body: Your readings. How much you move. What the evenings are made of. Whether you smoke. What runs in your family. Your age. Some of those move and some don't, and knowing which is which is worth more than a figure. Putting them together into an assessment needs a clinician with your notes in front of them — that's a consultation, and this isn't one.

blocks.title: Why the dates are on the front
blocks.body: Anything not checked in eighteen months comes down rather than sitting here looking current.

blocks.title: What this library will never contain
blocks.body: No medicine named for you, no change to one you already take, no score, no grade, no percentage, no traffic light on a reading. These pieces explain, and they haven't seen your notes.

S10.footer: Reviewed before it goes up, and dated so you can see how old it is.

S12.title: Support
S12.headline: A route to a person.
S12.sub: Nothing is sent until you preview it and confirm.

blocks.title: Call 911 now if any of these
blocks.body: Chest pain or pressure. Trouble speaking or understanding. Weakness or numbness down one side, or a drooping face. Sudden trouble seeing, or a sudden severe headache unlike your usual. Breathlessness at rest. Don't drive yourself, and don't take another reading first.

blocks.title: A reading well above your usual, and you feel fine
blocks.body: Sit five minutes, take it again, and ring Ahn Family Practice today with both numbers. SteadyBeat has no opinion about what they mean and will not offer one.

blocks.title: Six things stay on your phone.
blocks.body: Your mood ratings. How heavy the days felt. The symptom chips you ticked. Anything you typed in a note. Your reasons. Anything from any other program you're in — those are separate files and they are never pooled.

blocks.body: There's no summary line, no score, no flag on a reading, and no letter from us at the top. The practice gets your numbers and reads them itself.

S14.title: Settings & privacy

blocks.title: Notifications
blocks.body: Detail is off. A reminder on your lock screen says SteadyBeat and nothing else — not which program, not a reading, not why. Anyone who picks up your phone learns that an app reminded you. That's all, and that's the default.

items: Takeaway once instead of three times

blocks.title: Export everything
blocks.body: A readable file and a structured one: every reading, every check-in, every note, including the ones you've hidden from view. It stays on your phone unless you send it.

blocks.title: Delete everything
blocks.body: Completed, not hidden — your phone, our servers, and anything queued to sync. It can't be undone, and it ends your active programs.

Education and self-management support. It does not diagnose, treat or prescribe, does not calculate a clinical assessment of you, and is not a substitute for advice from a qualified health professional.

S14.footer: Changing your home number here changes nothing about your care. Tell your practice, not us.
